ROW.COLUMN: Money launderers often conduct intricate sequences of financial transactions that involve multiple accounts, institutions, and customers. The objective of performing a complex system of transactions is to make it difficult for investigators to trace the origin of the assets involved. This may be accomplished by establishing rings of accounts that appear to be unrelated, and then moving assets between several of these accounts. This scenario uses "link analysis" to uncover networks of unrelated customers, accounts, and external entities. These entities can be related by transactions or through shared common attributes such as common Tax ID, e-mail address, Phone Number, Address, and Password.
